repo_prior_art.cite: none; the Stat catalogue contains no rare-event PN coverage kernel

published_prior_art.cite: TianWu2025 gives regular PN efficient inference; ZhangWangMiao2025 gives PN-bound confidence intervals, not a rare-count cross-fitted point-PN inversion

TianWu2025 supplies the regular PN efficient limit and ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML supplies cross-fitted orthogonal-score Gaussian theory; the displayed triangular-array scaling is a plausible extension, not yet a distinct frontier object
CaiGuo2017 supplies an expected-length minimax template in high-dimensional regression; McGrathBurke2024 treats ordinary rare-binomial intervals, not learned PN-score inversion
GleserHwang1987 gives a general finite-expected-diameter impossibility and elementary rare-Bernoulli two-point arguments supply this lower-rate mechanism; PN specialization alone is incremental
Huwang1995 establishes non-uniform behavior of an asymptotic binomial interval near rare boundaries; the proposed multinomial Poisson-limit component needs a corrected causal connection
MikushevaSun2022 develops weak-IV test inversion, while no verified source supplies exact marked-Poisson calibration with cross-fitted PN nuisances

novelty_flags.label: project-level related work / thm:uniform-coverage
novelty_flags.one_line: The survey misses Zhang, Wang, and Miao, “Causal attribution with confidence” (arXiv:2504.08294), a closer PN-inference comparator that gives semiparametric efficiency theory and confidence intervals for PN bounds; it does not subsume this monotone rare-count target but must be compared explicitly.

soundness_flags.label: ass:localized-nuisance
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited regular DML condition does not establish the displayed rare-local weighted norm, r_0=o(sqrt(d_n)), or sqrt(n/d_n) r_e r_0=o(1); retag this as novel and justify or derive the needed conditions from primitive smoothness/sparsity assumptions.

soundness_flags.label: ass:localized-nuisance
soundness_flags.one_line: The load-bearing rare-local rate condition has no model class or learning guarantee showing it can hold in the proposed climate or medical regimes, and presently functions as an instrumental rate strengthening.

soundness_flags.label: thm:uniform-coverage / def:crossfit-score
soundness_flags.one_line: The assumption only asserts existence of estimators tilde-e and tilde-m_0, whereas the construction uses hat-eta without identifying it with them; it also gives no clipping/boundedness condition for the fitted propensity and regression, so the B_epsilon empirical-Bernstein bound need not apply to the fitted scores.

soundness_flags.label: def:least-favorable-law / thm:diameter-lower
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed least-favorable law is not a probability law unless d_n<=1/2, while ass:rare-event permits bar-d up to one; the lower bound also needs a stated nominal-level range such as alpha in (0,1/2).

soundness_flags.label: thm:poisson-boundary
soundness_flags.one_line: Under the stated least-favorable law only the rare cells have finite Poisson limits: the common treatment-by-outcome cell counts have means of order n and cannot jointly converge to finite independent Poisson variables; state the mixed Poisson/Gaussian experiment or restrict the assertion to rare cells.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:diameter-upper and thm:diameter-lower
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The lower result is only asserted on the explicit no-covariate least-favorable submodel, not by a full characterization of all laws in M_n.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The honest-diameter frontier is conditional on M_n containing the repaired least-favorable submodel; this is sufficient for a minimax lower bound against procedures honest over M_n.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Specify clipped fitted nuisances and foldwise conditional concentration, link hat-eta to the rate-certified learners, and rederive coverage with all nuisance-score perturbation terms controlled at the rare-event scale.

Replace the invalid all-cell Poisson claim with an explicit marked rare-cell point-process limit plus the Gaussian behavior of common cells, then show how that experiment yields the proposed inversion and diameter consequence.

Add ZhangWangMiao2025 to related work and sharpen the field contribution as the first honest rare-count point-PN interval/frontier under monotonicity, rather than presenting Gaussian recovery itself as a major strict extension.

recommended_next_step: Revise the fitted-score assumptions and boundary experiment, add the missing PN-inference comparator, then resubmit the repaired field-tier kernel for review.
